question.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion with damping. The position of the particle $y(t)$ at time $t$ is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+4{y}^{′}+20y=40\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.
$$

Which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for $y(t)?$

I. $y={e}^{-2t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡4t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)+10\operatorname{cos}⁡2t$

II. $y=R{e}^{-4t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+ϕ)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t$

III. $y=R{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
question.worked_solution:
The general solution is the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution:

$$
y(t)={y}_{c}(t)+{y}_{p}(t)
$$

First, we find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(t),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation ${y}^{″}+4{y}^{′}+20y=0.$ Writing down and solving the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +20 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4)-4+20 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2}+16 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =-16 \\ \lambda +2 & =\pm 4\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-2\pm 4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ can be expressed in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c}(t) & ={e}^{-2t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡4t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4t), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t).$ The particular solution is of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2t.
$$

By substituting the particular solution into the differential equation and equating coefficients, we find that $\alpha =2$ and $\beta =1.$ So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t.
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & ={e}^{-2t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡4t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Only III matches the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
